control.mechanism: An unwanted action requires a mismatched choice, execution and access, and failed prevention. Detection, escalation and actual stopping are distinct operations.
control.conditions: Keep C1/C2/C3 as joint conditions for L. Keep persistence and cross-organization spread as additional conditions for C4; neither awareness nor local cooperation suffices.
control.counterexample: A model can notice an evaluation yet fail to bypass restrictions; a human can terminate an unauthorized run before persistent control is lost.
control.evidence: Compared the new primary incident timelines, pre-action checks, action-aware monitoring, matched deployment simulation and AISI scope-clarification experiment with existing bounded control evidence.
control.limits: Simulation frequencies are not deployment incidence. Reported remediation is not independent effectiveness evidence. The DNS delay did not establish additional harm, so C3b retains its indirect level.
control.mitigation: Test least privilege, pre-execution checks, coverage, authenticated human approval, escalation and shutdown end to end. Preserve monitoring improvements and their remaining gaps.
control.readerContext: Both languages distinguish internal unnamed models, public model evaluations and real incidents. They introduce warning and shutdown separately before discussing the delay.
control.whyHere: These distinctions explain how local failures occur and where a defender can still stop them, without turning new reports into proof of global loss of control.

cyber.mechanism: Capability can support malicious operations only when users can obtain assistance and reach a target; target defenses and consequences require separate evidence.
cyber.conditions: Preserve M2c1 plus M2c2 and M3. Refusal, serving controls and open-weight configuration affect access independently of benchmark skill.
cyber.counterexample: An isolated exploit can succeed while the offered API refuses harmful assistance or the real target remains inaccessible.
cyber.evidence: Read Anthropic GLM-5.3 methods and denominators against the separate NIST CAISI methods, alongside existing observed misuse and intervention limits.
cyber.limits: 50/410 complete workflow attempts differs from best-of-three partial-credit scores. Simulated contact is not an intrusion. Commercial competitor evidence is not a neutral replication.
cyber.mitigation: Continue permission and connection limits, abuse detection and revocation. Record comparison conditions where service-side safeguards held.
cyber.readerContext: The text identifies who evaluates which model and what success means, without assuming that a reader knows benchmarks or tool simulations.
cyber.whyHere: M2c explains why more cyber capability can matter while M2c2 and M3 prevent capability from being read as inevitable harm.

primary.support: Bounded capability and access-condition tests; simulated contact and commercial-evaluator limits.
Different task inputs, best-of-three partial credit and actual ExploitGym denominator.
Real operations coexist with human involvement and platform intervention, not established global harm.

physical.mechanism: Assistance contributes to physical misuse only when harmful purpose, effective physical capability, materials/access and failed protection coincide.
physical.conditions: Maintain M1, M2b1/M2b2 and M3 as distinct conditions. A useful answer is not a fielded harmful device or biological event.
physical.counterexample: An attempted real field test can fail; a credentialed research user can obtain legitimate assistance without harmful purpose.
physical.evidence: Revisited the September threat report’s physical-outcome limits and LSVP access/monitoring terms; considered newer system-card capability tests without converting them to physical outcomes.
physical.limits: Developer knowledge evaluations and filtered observed activity do not estimate all-user prevalence. LSVP publishes no recall, response-time or harm-reduction comparison.
physical.mitigation: Applicant screening, scope restrictions, provider monitoring and organizational response can act at different stages; their effectiveness remains to be measured.
physical.readerContext: The existing text separates support for a task from making, accessing and deploying a physical system, including human involvement.
physical.whyHere: This prevents an increase in technical assistance from being mistaken for confirmation of the entire misuse route.

primary.locator: Physical operations and failed field-test discussion
primary.support: Observed attempts do not establish an operational device or widespread harm.

bio-defense.mechanism: A provenance signal may inform screening, but preventing harm also requires usable screening decisions, uptake, response and robustness.
bio-defense.conditions: M3 retains prevention, containment and recovery conditions; biological watermarking is one possible layer, not a complete barrier.
bio-defense.counterexample: A design can have known provenance and still be used unsafely, or originate from a tool outside the watermarking scheme.
bio-defense.evidence: Read the original Nature paper’s abstract, experimental framing, robustness and biosecurity discussion, alongside the authors’ announcement.
bio-defense.limits: Preserved utility and detectable marks in tested designs do not show deployment-level harm reduction. Deliberate manipulation and out-of-scope tools remain limitations.
bio-defense.mitigation: Combine provenance with access controls and screening; evaluate operational decisions and harm outcomes rather than treating the mark as a safety certificate.
bio-defense.readerContext: The added paragraph first explains the mark as a way to identify a design’s source, then states what this does not establish.
bio-defense.whyHere: It supplies concrete defensive progress at the point where the route asks whether prevention and containment can interrupt harm.

primary.locator: Abstract, Main, robustness; Discussion / Biosecurity perspective
primary.support: Technical proof of concept with preserved tested utility, not demonstrated prevention of misuse.

research.mechanism: A useful research contribution accelerates development only when it relieves a whole-project bottleneck; recursive improvement also requires successive gains to transfer and persist.
research.conditions: Keep research assistance, whole-process acceleration, RSI, ASI and safety research separate. Human supervision and validation remain part of the measured processes.
research.counterexample: A successful calculation can use known methods and later human checking without creating a self-improving AI-development cycle.
research.evidence: Re-read Anthropic development measurements, external METR Opus assessment and automated alignment findings; compared Nine Loops and the new restricted-access Argon announcement as bounded supporting examples.
research.limits: AL4 is not fully autonomous successor development. Five-task external testing over ten business days is not broad alignment verification. Unequal human iteration budgets limit safety-research comparisons.
research.mitigation: Use independent checking, held-out tasks, outcome measures, reproducibility and explicit accounting of human work and validation time.
research.readerContext: The tour explains what researchers do before discussing whether any one contribution speeds the whole process. Safety research remains a separate beneficial use.
research.whyHere: The retained branching avoids presenting research progress as either inevitable catastrophe or proof that defenses will keep pace.

capability.mechanism: Improved methods and compute use can raise capability; transfer to unfamiliar whole workflows is an additional condition.
capability.conditions: Preserve R0–C2a and R0–W1 transfer, exception, cost and intervention conditions. Broad superiority is separate from success in a single task family.
capability.counterexample: An agent can solve a well-specified software task while failing workplace coordination or physical requirements.
capability.evidence: Read current METR horizon definitions, human-time measurement and extrapolation caveats, plus the Chinchilla abstract as a non-RSI improvement example.
capability.limits: Human task duration is neither autonomous runtime nor a whole-job replacement probability. Older measurements do not fix a current capability ceiling.
capability.mitigation: Test complete workflows and exceptions with recorded interventions; bound authority separately from skill.
capability.readerContext: Both languages explain whose time is being measured and what parts of practical work remain untested.
capability.whyHere: Capability is introduced because it can change execution, research and work, while it does not determine goals or outcomes by itself.

primary.support: Human-duration task measure with limited domains and generalization.
Training allocation improvements without requiring a recursive-development loop.

work.mechanism: Technical ability affects adoption through cost and reliability; household welfare additionally depends on access, labor demand, ownership and distribution.
work.conditions: Maintain W1/W2 for technical all-labor replacement and the separate W3/W6 distribution route. Full replacement is not necessary for living without wages.
work.counterexample: Automation can assist employed people or raise output while displaced households receive none of the gain.
work.evidence: Compared the robot study’s task coding, environment distinctions and cost model with ILO exposure, Census adoption and IMF distribution framing. Inspected the robot cost figure in the PDF.
work.limits: 34% and 0.3% are model-based work-hour estimates, not realized replacement. Census firm and employment-weighted rates have different denominators and an older observation window.
work.mitigation: Measure actual costs, oversight, adoption and access to essentials; track household distribution rather than relying on aggregate technical potential.
work.readerContext: W2 labels the evidence as estimates before giving numbers and explains supervision and repairs. NOW preserves publication-versus-observation dates.
work.whyHere: The comparison clarifies why a technically possible task does not imply affordable deployment or universal income gains.

transactions.mechanism: Useful work or negotiation creates income only when someone pays and a transaction is authorized, fulfilled and profitable after costs.
transactions.conditions: Maintain I1a/I1b, fulfillment and cost conditions; ownership and distribution remain separate for I2.
transactions.counterexample: Agents can agree to exchange books even when a person never delivers a book; agreement creates no measured cash profit.
transactions.evidence: Read Project Swap setup, preference elicitation, limitations and delivery failures, alongside Project Vend’s actual tools and human purchase approval.
transactions.limits: Employee barter with low stakes and nonresponse is not a representative profit study. Vend changed models and scaffolding together, so gains are not isolated model effects.
transactions.mitigation: Check authorization, identity, fulfillment, disputes and net costs; maintain human approval where required.
transactions.readerContext: Both languages explain barter before distinguishing it from income, and delivery before stating why agreements are insufficient.
transactions.whyHere: This makes I1b’s real-world execution requirement concrete without treating trading-agent success as proof of universal agent income.

primary.support: 201-employee barter and some failed delivery, not demonstrated profit.
Improved commercial performance with scaffolding and human purchase authorization.

finance.mechanism: AI-supported actions can amplify financial disruptions only when they reach important operations and exceed buffers and recovery capacity.
finance.conditions: Keep F1/F2/F4 as joint conditions for F3. Cyber misuse and correlated decisions remain overlapping alternative mechanisms, not an inevitable chain.
finance.counterexample: A firm can use AI without autonomous trading; firms can share a provider yet make different trades; recovery can contain a local outage.
finance.evidence: Revisited BoE/FCA survey categories, FSB risk-channel/monitoring summaries and BIS FSI defense/recovery policy analysis.
finance.limits: Adoption is not traded value, concentration is not synchronized judgment, and policy analysis is not an observed AI-caused financial crisis.
finance.mitigation: Maintain transaction limits, independent checks, provider contingencies, buffers and restoration drills; include defensive AI without assuming it replaces these.
finance.readerContext: The existing text explains financial functions, liquidity and amplification with ordinary examples and bounded survey dates.
finance.whyHere: These distinctions keep the finance route separate from income distribution, the role of money and global existential harm.

primary.support: Adoption and limited autonomous use, not market-wide control.
Concentration, correlation and governance risks, not measured crisis causation.
Proposed monitoring and remaining measurement limits.

publication.mechanism: The update adds evidence within existing conditional routes and preserves the distinction between scientific findings and editorial connections.
publication.conditions: No topology, AND/OR requirements or evidence levels change; only substantively rechecked nodes and edges receive explanation dates.
publication.counterexample: A source can be newly available while reporting an old incident, a simulated result or a plan rather than a current outcome.
publication.evidence: Checked new source metadata, related nodes and connections, generated Japanese/English reading output, and stable-ID history translation alignment.
publication.limits: This editorial review is not independent replication, an exhaustive survey or a measurement of extinction probability. Initial publication dates remain null when only an update date is known.
publication.mitigation: Keep explicit limits, source provenance, review intervals and human review before merge. Record excluded and duplicate leads in the companion Markdown.
publication.readerContext: The introductory text explains the purpose, and the revised details explain incidents, simulations and modeled estimates without requiring glossary navigation.
publication.whyHere: The history and dependent routes help readers understand which evidence changed and why the causal interpretation remains conditional.
